newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hostage-takers reported off Nigerian barge.
newsitem.headline: Hostage-takers reported off Nigerian barge.

text.p: The hostage crisis aboard an oil barge in Nigeria appeared to have ended on Thursday, and a spokeswoman for the French oil contracting firm ETPM said there were no longer any unauthorised people on board.

"All I can say is that the barge has resumed moving toward the sea and the only people aboard are its 20 expatriate and 70 local employees. We don't know exactly what happened to lead to this but there are no more unauthorised people aboard," the ETPM spokeswoman told Reuters.

Reports from Lagos earlier said delicate negotiations were underway to try to free the crew from local people demanding jobs, although the Nigerian government said no foreigners had been taken hostage and the barge had been freed by the intervention of security agents.
"I don't know anything about security agents or rescue operations and cannot immediately check because we don't have radio contact for the moment," the spokeswoman said.
"But indeed there were people aboard before with whom we were negotiating about employment and they are no longer aboard," she said.
She said the crisis began on Tuesday when the barge was boarded by people seeking to be employed by the oil firm.
"We currently employ people from one community near where we work and the boarders resented not being included," she told Reuters. "We can't employ everybody."
ETPM went through a similar crisis last Christmas when 28 of its foreign workers including 10 Filipinos and nine Frenchmen were held on a barge offshore by 60 Nigerian workers demanding higher wages.
The expatriates involved this time were 16 Frenchmen, three Britons and an American, she said.
The latest incident was in the Escravos area off the western oil coastal town of Warri.
Communities in oil-producing areas have long been restive over lack of modern amenities in regions responsible for Nigeria's oil wealth. Clashes with oil companies have been common.
